# Finding the Antiderivative of -3*exp(x)*cos(x)

## Step 1: Use the known integral formula

I know that ∫exp(x)*cos(x) dx can be found using integration by parts twice.

## Step 2: Integration by parts

Let I = ∫exp(x)*cos(x) dx

**First application:** Let u = cos(x), dv = exp(x)dx
- du = -sin(x)dx, v = exp(x)

$$I = \text{exp}(x)\cos(x) + \int \text{exp}(x)\sin(x)\, dx$$

**Second application** on ∫exp(x)*sin(x)dx: Let u = sin(x), dv = exp(x)dx
- du = cos(x)dx, v = exp(x)

$$\int \text{exp}(x)\sin(x)\, dx = \text{exp}(x)\sin(x) - \int \text{exp}(x)\cos(x)\, dx = \text{exp}(x)\sin(x) - I$$

## Step 3: Solve for I

$$I = \text{exp}(x)\cos(x) + \text{exp}(x)\sin(x) - I$$
$$2I = \text{exp}(x)\cos(x) + \text{exp}(x)\sin(x)$$
$$I = \frac{\text{exp}(x)(\cos(x) + \sin(x))}{2}$$

## Step 4: Multiply by -3

$$\int -3\text{exp}(x)\cos(x)\, dx = -\frac{3}{2}\text{exp}(x)\cos(x) - \frac{3}{2}\text{exp}(x)\sin(x) + C$$

<answer>-3*exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x))/2 + C</answer>
